statutes_cited: West Pakistan Family Courts Act (XXXV of 1964)

full_text:
P L D 1991 Lahore 51

Before Malik Muhammad Qayyum, J

MUHAMMAD KHALIL‐‐Petitioner

versus

Mst. ZAHIDA PERVEEN and others‐‐Respondents

Writ Petition No.7245 of 1990, heard on 24th November, 1990.

(a) Punjab Court Fees (Abolition) Ordinance (X of 1983)‐‐

‐‐‐‐S. 2‐‐‐West Pakistan Family Courts Act (XXXV of 1964), Ss. 3 & 19‐‐‐Suit for maintenance‐ ‐‐Amount of maintenance awarded by Family Court was less than Rs.25,000‐‐‐No court‐fee was payable on memorandum of appeal and appeal could not be dismissed for failure to make up deficiency in court‐fee.

Provision of S.2, Punjab Court Fees (Abolition) Ordinance, 1983 provides that no court‐fee is chargeable in respect of any civil case, the value of the subject matter of which, does not exceed Rs.25,000. This concession according to the explanation is available at all stages of the case and before all Courts.

The appeal is a continuation of the suit and is a stage in the same case. The question as to whether the Family Court is a Court also does not present any difficulty. Section 3 of the Punjab Family Courts Act, 1964 empowers the Government to establish Family Courts and to appoint a Judge for each of such Courts. It is thus obvious that the Family Court is a Court and matter falling within its jurisdiction is entrusted to it in its capacity as a Court and not as a persona designata. [p. 54] A

In view of section 2 of Ordinance X of 1983, no court‐fee was payable on the memorandum of appeal filed by the petitioner and the appeal could not be dismissed for failure to make up the deficiency in court‐fee. [p. 54) B

Mirza Daud Baig v. Additional District Judge, Gujranwala and others 1987 SCMR 1161 ref.

Mst. Gaman v. Taj Din PLD 1968 Lah. 987; Hussain Bakhsh v. Settlement Commissioner, Rawalpindi and others PLD 1970 SC 1; Mirza Daud Baig v. Additional District Judge, Gujranwala and others 1987 SCMR 1161;

Muhammad Anwar Khan v. Additional District Judge, Rawalpindi and others PLD 1978 Lah. 716 and Abdul Ghafoor v. Muhammad Rafiq and others PLD 1983 Lah. 383 ref.

(b) West Pakistan Family Courts Act (XXXV of 1964)--

----Ss. 5 & 14---Constitution of Pakistan (1973), Art. 199---Appeal against decree for maintenance---Certified copy of decree of Family Court not filed in appeal--Effect---Memorandum of appeal having not been rejected on such ground, same was not required to be decided in Constitutional jurisdiction---Respondent, however, would have option to raise such objection before Appellate Court in the post remand proceedings which had been ordered by the High Court---Case was remanded for decision afresh in accordance with law. [p. 54] C

(c) West Pakistan Family Courts Act (XXXV of 1964)--

----S. 3---Punjab Court Fees (Abolition) Ordinance (X of 1983), S. 2---Family Court is a Court for the purposes of S.2 of Punjab Court Fees (Abolition) Act, 1983 and not a persona designata---Family Court is a Civil Court in every sense despite the exclusion of the Code of Civil Procedure and the Evidence Act , 1872 in their application to proceedings before such a Court and notwithstanding having been created by a special statute and mentioned in the Act as distinct from Civil Court. [p. 54] A & D

Mirza Daud Baig v. Additional District Judge, Gujranwala and others 1987 SCMR 1161 and Muhammad Anwar Khan v. Additional District Judge, Rawalpindi and others PLD 1978 Lah. 716 ref.

Muhammad Shaukat Hashmi for Petitioner. Pervaiz 1. Mir for Respondent No.l. Nemo for Respondents Nos.2 and 3.

Date of hearing: 24th November, 1990.
